regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY and PMI Composite at 55.9 look unambiguous — until you note that core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY while capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is only at the 74th percentile, not the 85th+ that historically triggers private capex commitments. The quality question: IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY is real, but commercial vehicle sales falling for two consecutive months to 12.6% YoY suggests goods movement is not confirming the investment story. Growth is genuine but narrower than the headline implies — services and government capex are carrying weight that private manufacturing has not yet picked up.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY is uncomfortable; fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile reading — is the structural problem. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY sits well below headline, which means the RBI can tell itself the underlying trend is benign. The inversion: if Brent at $110.65/bbl stays flat and the INR at 95.24 holds, fuel inflation mechanically eases in six months. But if either leg slips — crude up $10 or INR down 3% — the RBI's 5.1% YoY inflation forecast becomes a floor, not a ceiling, and the extended pause becomes a credibility problem.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY is a 160 bps divergence that has widened for two consecutive months. The CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits has eased from 83% but remains at the 73rd percentile historically — and the last time it sustained above 80% while the repo rate was on hold, the RBI responded with macro-prudential tightening on risk weights within three quarters. Services credit at 24.3% YoY and NBFC credit at 15.8% YoY are the pressure points: both are accelerating into a funding base that is not keeping pace. Watch for a risk-weight circular before a rate move.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, and the RBI's own GDP forecast of 6.7% YoY sits 110 bps below the actual 7.8% YoY print — a gap that historically precedes upward forecast revisions, not rate cuts. Real repo rate against headline CPI is effectively negative at -29 bps; against core CPI it is +135 bps. The RBI is threading a needle: too tight for housing affordability (avg home loan rate at 7.35% p.a.), too loose for a fuel-driven inflation overshoot. The extended pause is not neutral — it is a bet that fuel inflation is transitory and credit stress is manageable. Both bets are live.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY rising from 16.1% YoY, and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — the highest in 18 months — are the two cleanest signals that the investment cycle is real. The contradiction: core sector growth at 4.8% YoY is decelerating, and commercial vehicle sales have fallen two consecutive months to 12.6% YoY. Goods movement and infrastructure throughput are not confirming the capital goods surge. The most likely explanation is that capex is concentrated in IT, telecom, and logistics (services credit at 24.3% YoY supports this) rather than broad-based industrial expansion. Private manufacturing capex is still waiting for utilisation to clear 80%.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹203,521 cr / month is at the 73rd percentile and stable — neither a demand surge nor a fade. Passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY have fallen two consecutive months from 26.1% YoY, which is the sharpest deceleration in the dataset and the most important consumption signal today. Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY are strong, pointing to rural and mass-market demand holding. The divergence — premium urban (PV) decelerating while mass-market (2W) accelerates — is the classic dual-economy split: affluent urban consumers are pausing, possibly on affordability and rate sensitivity, while rural demand is recovering from a low base. E-commerce GMV growth at 12.4% YoY at the 15th percentile confirms the urban discretionary softness.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 57th percentile. Services credit surging at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile), rising 2 straight months.","implication":"The deposit acceleration masks structural stress: retail deposits are growing, but wholesale funding gaps are widening for smaller banks and NBFCs. Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% and deposit-to-liability ratios >70%; avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities. Watch for RBI to signal liquidity tightening via CRR hikes or OMO drains within 6 weeks. Credit growth will moderate to 14-16% by Q3 as funding constraints bite.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile is elevated but not crisis-level; historically, ratios >85% preceded NBFC stress (2018-19). Current divergence is manageable if deposit growth sustains above 15% YoY.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Beyond Cyclicals","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest, up from 16.1% YoY), now at 52nd percentile. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), at 74th percentile — highest in 18 months. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5% YoY but still neutral). Services credit at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile, rising 2 months) signals capex in IT, telecom, and logistics. Vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY (68th percentile, rising 2 months) — commercial vehicle sales at 12.6% YoY but falling 2 straight months.","implication":"Capex is broadening from traditional heavy industry into services and logistics. Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Escorts, Bharat Electronics) and IT infrastructure plays (Tata Communications, Sterlite Tech). Underweight auto OEMs until CV sales stabilise; the divergence between credit growth and unit sales suggests financing-driven demand, not organic capex. Expect IIP capital goods to sustain 14-18% through Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the inflection point where capex ROI turns positive; historically, sustained >76% utilisation preceded 18-24 months of capex acceleration (2014-16, 2021-22).","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 93rd Percentile, But Ticket Size Rising","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (latest), at 93rd percentile, rising 3 consecutive months (₹29,845→₹31,961→₹32,297→₹32,490 cr / month). SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (down from 10.45 mn, at 2nd percentile — data quality issue). SIP AUM at ₹17.86 lakh cr (39th percentile, up 2 of last 3 months). Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (80th percentile, up 2 of last 3 months). But SIP YoY growth at 10.7% (30th percentile, down from 15% YoY) — growth is decelerating.","implication":"SIP inflows are strong in absolute terms, but growth is slowing and average ticket size is rising (SIP AUM +₹1.66 lakh cr while accounts fell 390k). This is late-cycle behaviour: affluent retail entering via SIPs, not mass-market expansion. Equity MF net inflows remain robust at ₹38,307 cr / month, but NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) — new fund launches are dead. Maintain overweight on large-cap, dividend-paying equities; avoid small-cap and thematic funds where retail concentration is highest.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile are near all-time highs, but the deceleration in YoY growth (10.7% vs 15% a quarter ago) mirrors 2021 — a warning sign of retail saturation before corrections.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile, Brent Stable","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% YoY), at 95th percentile — the highest in the dataset. Brent crude at $110.65 / bbl (flat, 77th percentile). WTI at $101.93 / bbl (flat, 83rd percentile). Natural gas at $3.016 / MMBtu (flat, 18th percentile). Iron ore at $161.91 / t (up from $90.70 / t, 63rd percentile). Copper at $6.665 / lb (flat, 79th percentile). FAO food index at 136 index (up from 134.5, 61st percentile).","implication":"Fuel inflation is decoupled from crude prices — this is a refining margin and excise tax story, not a global oil shock. India's fuel subsidy withdrawal and higher GST on petroleum products are driving domestic inflation. Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) for margin expansion; underweight airlines (IndiGo, SpiceJet) and logistics (TCI Express) until fuel inflation moderates. Expect fuel inflation to remain elevated (18-24% YoY) through Q3 FY27 unless crude falls below $95 / bbl or excise is cut.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is unsustainable and typically precedes RBI rate cuts (2020-21, 2023-24). If headline CPI remains >5.5% for 2 more months, RBI will signal a pause-to-cut cycle.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"BOJ Tightening Breaks Carry Trade Consensus","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (up from 1% p.a.), at 100th percentile — highest in dataset. Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% p.a., 68th percentile), rising 2 in a row. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (up from 2.25% p.a., 63rd percentile), rising 2 in a row. US 10Y Treasury at 4.99% yield (down from 5%, 90th percentile). DXY at 102.239 index (flat, 56th percentile, up 4 of last 5 months). US PMI composite at 58.4 index (91st percentile, rising 2 months). Global PMI composite at 54.3 index (84th percentile, rising 2 months).","implication":"BOJ's rate hikes are the first major central bank tightening in a synchronized global expansion. This breaks the carry trade consensus (borrow yen, invest in EM equities). FII flows to India will remain volatile; expect ₹5,000-10,000 cr / month outflows if DXY sustains >102 and US 10Y yields stay >4.9%. Reduce leverage in EM portfolios; hedge INR exposure via forwards or put spreads. Overweight USD-denominated assets and US equities (S&P 500 at 100th percentile) until BOJ signals a pause.","pct_10y":100,"pct_note":"BOJ at 100th percentile is a regime shift — the first time in 15 years that Japan is tightening while the Fed is on pause. This historically precedes EM currency weakness and equity volatility.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"INR Stable, But FII Outflows Accelerating","data_text":"INR at 95.24 ₹ / USD (flat, 89th percentile, up 2 of last 5 months). FII equity net at -₹49,935 cr / month (latest, 17th percentile, mild-negative signal). DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile, up 2 of last 3 months). India VIX at 16.245 index (12th percentile, down from 16.4, strong-positive signal). Nifty 50 at 22,698.85 index (73rd percentile, down from 22,749.75). Bank Nifty at 54,267.4 index (89th percentile, up from 53,974.8).","implication":"INR is holding at 95.24 because DII inflows (₹51,829 cr / month) are offsetting FII outflows (₹49,935 cr / month). This is a fragile equilibrium: if FII outflows exceed ₹60,000 cr / month, INR will weaken to 96-97 range. RBI is likely intervening via spot sales or forward guidance. Maintain INR hedges for 3-6 month horizon; avoid long INR positions. Overweight domestic-focused equities (FMCG, retail, utilities) that benefit from INR weakness; underweight exporters (IT, pharma) until FII flows stabilise.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile is near all-time weakness; historically, sustained weakness >95.5 preceded RBI rate cuts and equity underperformance (2022-23).","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Weakness","data_text":"Office absorption at 15.08 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, 8th percentile, strong-negative signal of -84), down from 13.21 mn sq ft / quarter. Office vacancy at 14.8% vacant (43rd percentile, up from 14.5%). But Nifty IT index is flat (not collapsing), and India credit services at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile, rising 2 months). Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (7th percentile, strong-positive signal of +86), down from 5%. Airline passengers at 86.4 mn / month (35th percentile, mild-negative signal). E-commerce GMV growth at 12.4% YoY (15th percentile, strong-negative signal of -70, down from 18% YoY).","implication":"Office absorption is collapsing NOT because IT services are shrinking, but because Global Capability Centres (GCCs) are consolidating into fewer, larger campuses (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune). Traditional IT services firms (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are shedding leased office space as they shift to owned facilities and hybrid models. Meanwhile, retail malls are thriving (4.8% vacancy at 7th percentile) because e-commerce GMV growth is decelerating (12.4% YoY, down from 18%) — consumers are returning to physical retail. This is a structural shift: overweight retail REITs (Brookfield REIT, Mindspace REIT) and underweight office REITs (Embassy REIT). Services credit growth (24.3% YoY) is being driven by logistics, fintech, and GCC capex, NOT traditional IT services. Falsifiable: if Nifty IT falls >15% in next 3 months, this thesis breaks.","pct_10y":8,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 8th percentile is a 10-year low, but retail vacancy at 7th percentile is also a 10-year low — the divergence signals a structural reallocation of commercial real estate demand, not a cyclical downturn.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, But the Goods Economy Is Sending a Different Signal

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY (64th percentile) with PMI Composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) — both above trend.
  • But passenger vehicle sales fell to 7.9% YoY for the second consecutive month (from 26.1% YoY), and commercial vehicle sales dropped to 12.6% YoY for the second consecutive month — goods movement is not confirming the headline.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY (61st percentile) signal rural demand is intact, creating a sharp urban-rural split.
  • Core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0% YoY — infrastructure throughput decelerating even as capital goods IIP accelerates.

The tension: GDP and PMI signal broad expansion; vehicle sales and core sector signal that the goods economy is softening at the margin. Services are carrying growth that manufacturing has not yet validated.

Bottom line: Watch PV sales for a third consecutive monthly decline — that would confirm urban discretionary is turning, not just normalising from a high base.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US 10Y Retreats to 4.99% — Relief Rally or the Calm Before BOJ Forces the Issue

The facts:

  • US 10Y Treasury at 4.99% yield (90th percentile), down 1 bp — the first move lower after five sessions near 5.15%.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile of the dataset), rising for the second consecutive meeting — yen carry unwind is structural, not episodic.
  • US PMI Composite at 58.4 (91st percentile, rising two months) contradicts US GDP SAAR at 2.2% SAAR (50th percentile) — surveys are pricing re-acceleration that nominal output has not delivered.
  • But Eurozone CPI at 3.8% YoY (rising two months) with ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (rising two months) means DM central banks are tightening in unison for the first time since mid-2023.

The tension: DM survey data prices growth re-acceleration; actual GDP and yield curve price deceleration. BOJ at a 10-year-high rate is the underappreciated transmission mechanism — every 25 bps of BOJ tightening unwinds another leg of the carry trade that has funded EM inflows.

Bottom line: If US 10Y breaks back above 5.10% yield on the next payrolls print, the 1 bp relief today is noise — position for INR and FII pressure to resume.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds, But the Institutional Conviction Gap Is Widening

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising for three consecutive months — retail allocation is systematic and sticky.
  • But SIP YoY growth at 10.7% YoY (30th percentile), down from 15.0% YoY — the flow is large but the growth rate is decelerating.
  • FII equity net at -₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile) — the largest monthly outflow in the recent sequence, offset almost exactly by DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile).
  • NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) — institutional product launches have effectively stopped, signalling fund house caution on near-term market direction.

The tension: Retail SIP flows are providing near-perfect DII offset to FII selling — but this equilibrium depends on SIP growth not decelerating further. NFO collapse at the 2nd percentile suggests the industry itself is not confident enough to launch new products into this market.

Bottom line: Watch monthly SIP inflows: a print below ₹31,000 cr / month would signal retail conviction is cracking, removing the only reliable FII offset.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 89th Percentile, REITs Collapsing — Two Markets, One Credit Story

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 2 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Hyderabad are the primary destinations, supported by remittances at $144.8 bn (16.2% YoY).
  • Hyderabad leads city momentum: sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, price +6% YoY, 28 months unsold inventory — supply is running ahead of demand.
  • Office absorption at 15.08 mn sq ft / quarter (8th percentile) with GCCs taking 41% of occupier mix — the headline weakness masks a structural shift from IT services to GCC-led demand.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down sharply from prior prints — the listed office market is pricing the absorption weakness, not the GCC narrative.

The tension: Residential demand is bifurcated: NRI and premium buyers are active, mass-market is soft. Office absorption is structurally shifting to GCCs, but REIT prices are discounting the transition period, not the destination.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption sustains above 18 mn sq ft / quarter for two consecutive quarters; overweight residential developers with Hyderabad and Bengaluru exposure.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Fuel, BOJ, and Credit Stress

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, rising from 20.05% YoY) with Brent at $110.65/bbl — every $10 crude increase widens CAD by ~40 bps and feeds back into CPI with a two-quarter lag.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — yen carry unwind is accelerating; FII equity outflows at -₹49,935 cr / month are the first-order effect, INR pressure is the second.
  • Bank credit at 19.4% YoY vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for two consecutive months; CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits (73rd percentile) is the macro-prudential tripwire.
  • But India VIX at 16.245 (12th percentile) suggests the market is not yet pricing any of these risks — complacency is itself a risk.

The tension: Each of the three risks is individually manageable; the danger is sequencing — a Brent spike widens CAD, weakens INR, accelerates FII outflows, tightens domestic liquidity, and forces the RBI's hand on rates precisely when credit stress is peaking.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a sustained break above $115/bbl triggers the full cascade — CAD, INR, FII, and RBI response — simultaneously.

"}
